title: Ripple, operating modes, and component selection

lessons.title: Inductor ripple, peaks, valleys, and boundaries
lessons.physicalIntuition: Inductance resists slope, not current itself. Higher switching frequency or L reduces triangular excursion; load shifts the triangle vertically until a unidirectional stage touches zero.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Integrate each ideal slope over on/off intervals to derive Delta iL. In symmetric steady triangular ripple, Ipk/val = Iavg ± Delta/2 and boundary load equals Delta/2 for a unidirectional ideal buck.
lessons.modelingConsequence: The sandbox must distinguish analytical fixed-frequency CCM estimates from event-driven switched results, and detect zero-current mode transitions rather than clamping after the fact.
assumptions: ideal fixed-frequency timing for closed-form ripple
lessons.transferQuestion: Halve L and double phase count at the same total load: what happens to each phase's ripple ratio and boundary load?

lessons.title: Capacitive, ESR, ESL, and multiphase ripple
lessons.physicalIntuition: Capacitance integrates current mismatch, ESR turns current directly into voltage, and ESL turns current edge rate into voltage. Interleaving changes the summed current before these impedance elements act.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: For ideal single-phase CCM triangular capacitor current, Delta vC ≈ Delta iL/(8 C fs). Lumped ESR adds iC RESR and ESL adds LESL diC/dt; waveform components need not peak together.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Store ideal capacitor voltage separately from terminal output voltage. Label lumped ESL as educational, and warn that edge ringing/probe loops are not captured by a single element.
lessons.transferQuestion: Why can two capacitors with the same C yield different edge ripple and different low-frequency droop?

lessons.title: Nonideal state equations and loss intuition
lessons.physicalIntuition: Series drops reduce the voltage available to change current and dissipate energy. Dead-time diode conduction can dominate a short interval even when MOSFET resistance is small.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Replace ideal switch-node/inductor voltage with Vin - Vo - iL(RHS+RDCR) on, and approximately -Vo - iL(RLS+RDCR) during low-side conduction; use the sign-aware diode clamp in dead time. Conduction loss uses RMS current squared times resistance under stated temperature.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Each phase exposes resistances and diode drop separately, allowing voltage error, slope change, and dissipation estimates. Do not claim switching loss without charge/capacitance/gate dynamics.
lessons.transferQuestion: Which resistance changes DC conversion error and which measurement would separate it from timing error?

lessons.title: Load-step charge and design trade space
lessons.physicalIntuition: Load current can jump; inductor current cannot. The capacitor supplies the deficit until phases slew, so smaller ripple is not automatically faster transient response.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Integrate Delta i(t) = iload - sum(iL) over the deficit window to get Delta Q and Delta V ≈ Delta Q/C before including ESR, ESL, and loop recovery. Bound di/dt from available inductor voltage and per-phase current limits.
lessons.modelingConsequence: The operating-point designer scores voltage droop, ripple, current stress, and slew feasibility separately. Multiple valid L/C/fs/N choices remain possible.
assumptions: charge-deficit estimate omits full closed-loop recovery
lessons.transferQuestion: Defend two designs: one with low ripple/high L and one with faster current slew/lower L. Which needs more current-limit margin?

lessons.title: Waveform identification without label guessing
lessons.physicalIntuition: A waveform label follows from conduction paths and event rules. A flat zero-current interval means something different from negative forced-synchronous current, and isolated jagged samples may be numerical rather than physical.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Test whether iL stays positive, reaches zero only at a boundary, remains at zero for a finite interval, or crosses negative while a bidirectional path is enabled. Check event/timestep convergence and state-equation residuals before assigning a physical instability label.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Generated identification cases preserve hidden ground truth: switch states, event log, timestep, and mode policy. Explanations reveal these after the learner commits.
assumptions: mode labels use the project's declared current sign and conduction policy
lessons.transferQuestion: What extra evidence distinguishes pulse skipping from a simulator that stepped over a narrow pulse?
